doc.title: Ruth & Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Saddle River, New Jersey, January 19, 2015

title: Contractors calling the house and checking in by phone
summary: Ruth and Bucky explain why contractors avoided talking to wives, the Radio Registry, and checking in from pay phones.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: I wanted to go back to, Ruth, something you said when the contractors called the house looking for Bucky that sometimes they didn’t really want to talk to you. How come, do you know?
Well they don’t want to give the information to the wife, thinking that the wife won’t tell the husband.
No, they made me feel like I didn’t know what to do or how to say it or who to get, and they’d say no, I’ll call back. It didn’t happen very often.
When you hire someone you’ve got to go direct.
Yeah. Like they want to know you’ve got to bring your Strat or whatever.
Well did you ever feel like you might be losing out on work because he wasn’t there to get that call?
Oh no, no, no. Never, never.
They were all right. They were pretty good.
So after a date ended, if you had a 10-1 or something and you had an hour, did you head for the phones to check in.
Yeah. I always checked in with her.
But you guys had to find a pay phone, right?
How did it ever happen before cell phones?
I don’t know how they did it.
